purpose: Authoritative-vendor manufacturing execution integration delta promoting Aegis FactoryLogix at spec-verified only. Reuses the existing HTTP RPC/JSON and files/SFTP profiles for xTend JSON and xStream/XML/file export routes, records the on-prem cleartext-default endpoint and mutative RPC authority as security evidence blockers, and keeps Manufacturing WFM read-only and customer-edge constrained. No customer credentials, production data, write/control calls or plant-network probes were used.

patch.name: Aegis FactoryLogix
securityEvidenceBlockers: The documented xTend REST JSON/POX examples use an on-prem http://[server]:6063 endpoint and username/password Connect flow. WFM must not send credentials or customer data over cleartext HTTP or directly traverse a protected plant network; authentication evidence cannot advance until the customer exposes a verified TLS-protected edge/read projection or another customer-approved encrypted route.

xTend is a session-backed method API that includes mutative production, configuration, security and equipment/automation operations as well as reads. A dedicated non-admin FactoryLogix identity, effective read-only role evidence and an explicit reviewed read-method allowlist (or the one-way xStream/export route) are required before authentication can count as safe WFM evidence.
patch.evidenceNote: Aegis documents FactoryLogix xTend as a direct integration API and xStream as a one-way automated export path. The xTend REST interface exposes JSON and XML/POX service/method URLs, establishes a session with FactoryLogix credentials and a database connection, then requires the returned sessionId on subsequent calls. FactoryLogix roles have individually configurable permissions, while xTend includes mutative methods such as deleting users and recording indirect touch time; HTTP method or session success therefore does not prove read-only authority. FactoryLogix also models factories/areas/lines/workstations, WIP tracking and touch time, operation resource restrictions, cycle/setup times, material/resource context and operation certification restrictions that validate operators against required current certifications. Customer Library access can be broad if no users/groups are associated with a customer, so customer/site scope must be explicitly proven. The same platform can connect equipment/automation; WFM deliberately consumes only the enterprise/read projection and does not inherit CFX/xLink, equipment, robot or control authority.

requiredPermissions: customer-edge only: no direct cloud scan or direct connection to an on-prem FactoryLogix xTend service
prefer one-way xStream/export where it supplies the approved dataset; validate checksums, schema, source timestamps and idempotent file ingestion
for xTend, dedicated non-admin FactoryLogix technical user with only the minimum effective read permissions required for approved services/methods

explicit reviewed allowlist of read-only xTend service/method identifiers; deny production mutation, user/security administration, process/product editing, material movement, equipment/automation actions and all other mutative methods
explicit factory/site/customer/database-connection binding; customer access must be constrained rather than relying on the permissive no-association default
TLS-protected customer edge, reverse proxy or equivalent encrypted transport before FactoryLogix credentials/session identifiers can be presented
no direct SQL integration: Aegis recommends xTend rather than bypassing FactoryLogix business logic
dataAvailableOrExpected: factory hierarchy including factories, areas, lines, workstations/clusters and resource/location identifiers
production batches/orders, WIP state, operations/routing context, start/finish/touch-time evidence and production status
operation estimated cycle time, setup time, resource restrictions and workstation/resource requirements
operator/user references and operation certification restrictions, including the requirement that operator certifications be valid before an operation proceeds
material, stock/resource, tooling/consumable and manufacturing-readiness context where exposed by the customer's approved projection
quality/inspection/non-conformance and traceability context where exposed by approved read services or xStream reports
machine/equipment and production context only through a governed FactoryLogix read projection; no direct CFX/xLink/PLC control path
automationOpportunities: compare planned/active FactoryLogix operations with WFM availability and verified qualifications to surface skill-constrained production risk before the shift starts
recommend qualified redeployment between lines/workstations when WIP, resource or disruption state changes, without changing FactoryLogix execution state
forecast overtime or agency-labour pressure from production backlog, cycle/setup expectations and the number of currently eligible workers

reconcile payable attendance with FactoryLogix operation/touch-time evidence to identify paid-but-nonproductive time and labour-to-order/unit cost, while keeping WFM/payroll authoritative for payable time
hold or reroute staffing recommendations when required material/tool/resource readiness is missing so labour is not sent to work that cannot start
use engineering/process/certification changes as a trigger for qualification-gap and retraining readiness review

future controlled write candidates exist through xTend, but all production, labour-time, user/security, material and equipment/control writes remain disabled until a separate authorised write-roundtrip programme
savingsHypotheses: reduce avoidable overtime and agency demand by finding skill-constrained production coverage gaps before work reaches the line
reduce paid idle time and throughput loss by redeploying appropriately qualified labour when WIP/resource conditions change
reduce qualification-related production delays by joining operation certification requirements to current WFM worker readiness before assignment
reduce labour-cost reconciliation effort by linking WIP/touch-time/production evidence to WFM time, shift and cost records without treating MES touch time as payroll truth
reduce wasted labour dispatch when materials, tooling or other required resources are not production-ready
reduce bespoke implementation effort by reusing the existing HTTP RPC/JSON operation-gating pattern and file-batch ingestion rather than creating a FactoryLogix-specific transport stack
dataGaps: FactoryLogix is not normally authoritative for employment contract, leave/absence, payable time, payroll rules, agency commercials or full workforce availability

FactoryLogix certification data may be authoritative for shop-floor process gating but does not automatically represent every legal, regulated or customer-defined WFM qualification; mapping authority must be explicit
public documentation does not establish a universal pagination, rate-limit or incremental-change contract for all xTend read methods; each approved method requires tenant/version proof
available xTend services depend on licences/version/deployment and customer role permissions; method availability must be discovered rather than assumed

multi-site deployments can use different database connections, customer associations, custom fields, process/resource identifiers and regional operating models that require versioned customer-specific mappings
xStream export content and cadence depend on the configured report/export; file completeness and freshness must be proven before real-time workforce decisions
constraintsRisks: the public xTend getting-started contract shows cleartext HTTP on port 6063; this is an evidence blocker, not an acceptable production WFM transport

xTend sessions are created with reusable FactoryLogix credentials and session identifiers; secrets/session IDs must remain executor-bound, encrypted in transit, rotated according to customer policy and absent from logs/evidence
the same API has read and mutative methods, including security and labour-time mutation; HTTP verb alone cannot classify authority and only reviewed read method IDs may be called
FactoryLogix customer access can be unexpectedly broad when no users/groups are associated with a customer; explicit customer/site scope proof is required before tenant evidence
Aegis supports SaaS, cloud, hybrid and on-prem deployments but the documented xTend service is server-oriented; endpoint topology and safe customer-edge placement must be discovered per deployment
equipment connectivity, CFX/xLink and factory automation capabilities are separate high-authority surfaces and must not be inherited by the WFM connector
intermittent plant connectivity, duplicate WIP/events, late file exports and schema/version drift must fail to stale/advisory mode rather than silently producing complete-looking staffing decisions
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing HTTP RPC/JSON and files-SFTP adapters. In an authorised non-production/customer environment, first prove an encrypted customer-edge route and a dedicated FactoryLogix technical user with explicitly reviewed read-only effective permissions and constrained customer/site/database scope; otherwise use a customer-controlled xStream one-way export. For xTend, inventory the exact installed-version service/method catalogue, allowlist only non-mutative read methods, prove attempted mutative methods fail, then validate method-specific paging/rate behaviour, session expiry/reconnect, multi-database/site identity, custom fields, schema fingerprints, stable-ID deduplication and WIP/touch-time/certification mappings. Do not call production, labour-time, user/security, material, equipment or automation mutations.
